links.outcome: ED length of stay and revisit rates before vs after AI fracture detection deployment, with internal control
links.effect: Mean F-E LOS fell 135.6 to 127.5 min (Δ -8.13; 95% CI -11.52 to -4.70); F-C control unchanged (Δ +0.37 min); interaction -7.99 min (p=0.004); early revisits did not increase.
links.quote: Mean F-E LOS decreased from 135.6 to 127.5 min (Δ -8.13 min; 95% CI -11.52 to -4.70; p < 0.001) and median LOS from 114.0 to 109.8 min (p < 0.001); the F-C control was unchanged (Δ + 0.37 min; 95% CI -3.95 to +4.74; p = 0.87); the cohort-by-period interaction was -7.99 min (95% CI -13.36 to -2.62; p = 0.004).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the operational impact (length of stay, revisit rates) of deploying an AI radiographic fracture detection tool in a real-world ED setting, but does not compare specific deployment practices or safeguards.
